relations.note: As a great serpent, Quetzalcoatl seizes and tears Tlaltecuhtli apart with Tezcatlipoca.
Tezcatlipoca helps restrain and dismember Tlaltecuhtli, forming earth and heaven from the body.
Horrified gods compensate Tlaltecuhtli by making useful plants and terrestrial features arise from the body.

relations.myth: Swallowing and birth of the sun
relations.note: Tlaltecuhtli swallows the setting sun, participates in its nocturnal transformation, and births it at dawn.
Some scholars identify the central face as Tlaltecuhtli or a combined earth-sun being rather than Tonatiuh alone.
Colonial authors sometimes apply Earth Lord terminology to Tlaloc, reflecting overlapping terrestrial, mountain, and water domains.
Some sources and retellings equate these overlapping earth-monster identities, while other colonial accounts distinguish them.
A Tlaltecuhtli form carved beneath Coatlicue materially joins the mother goddess with terrestrial support.
A colonial cosmogonic tradition pairs them as male and female earth powers, though their separateness varies.
This descriptive sacred-earth name is sometimes equivalent to Tlaltecuhtli, depending on the passage.
